episodes.187244: Rain spread into southeast Ohio on the morning of January 24th and continued through much of the day as a slow moving system entered the Middle Ohio Valley. Heaviest rain amounts occurred as the system moved by overnight, resulting in a swath of 1 to 2 inches of precipitation over southeastern Ohio. Additional water concerns were contributed by snow from a previous storm that was melting due to warmer temperatures during this time. ||Flooding began across portions of southeast Ohio the night of the 24th and continued into the next day as runoff from rain and snowmelt made its way into the creeks, streams, and smaller rivers. Light to moderate showers lingered through the morning of the 25th as renewed energy from a weak disturbance passed overhead. Additionally, another round of moderate to heavy rain pushed through with a surface low that evening. This subsequent round of precipitation tracked across the same, already saturated, portions of southeast Ohio which exacerbated ongoing flooding. Precipitation continued to progress northeast, exiting the area in the early morning hours on the 26th.||In Washington County, several roads were closed due to flooding and the following gages exceeded bankfull levels the morning of the 25th: Little Muskingum River at Bloomfield, Duck Creek at Macksburg, and Duck Creek below Whipple. In Meigs County, the Shade River at Chester and several other rivers and creeks also rose out of their banks, leading to multiple road closures. Additional road closures were reported across Athens, Gallia, and Vinton Counties during this time. Most creeks and streams gradually lowered back into their banks on the afternoon and evening of the 25th, though a few did not fall below bankfull until the next morning.

episodes.188472: An amplified upper level trough dropping out of the Rockies tracked east across the Central Plains. As it did so, it began to drive a cold front east through Texas and across the northern Gulf Coast. Ample moisture and sufficient instability enhanced intensity of a couple thunderstorms which resulted in a damaging wind report in Pearl River County.

Several rivers and creeks rose out of their banks in Meigs County, leading to multiple road closures. Across the central part of the county, flooding impacted portions of Kingsbury Road, Route 143, Route 124 from Dead Mans Curve Road to State Route 325, and Noble Summit Road near McElhinney Hill Road and Bradbury Road.

Golf ball sized hail reported by the public.

The gage at Macksburg along the West Fork of Duck Creek exceeded a bankfull level of 13 feet in the early morning hours of January 25th, then continued to rise to a crest just under 14 feet during the afternoon. The river lowered back into its banks that evening. Minor flooding along Main Street was observed during the time that the creek was out of its banks.

The gage along the Shade River near Chester exceeded its bankfull level of 16 feet during the early morning hours of January 25th. The river crested just over 17 feet late that night, then fell below bankfull once again early the next morning. Low lying spots along Scout Camp Road encountered high water issues as excessive water spilled onto the roadways while the river was out of its banks.

The Little Muskingum River gage at Bloomfield exceeded its bankfull level of 16 feet during the early morning hours of January 25th. The river crested just under 20 feet during the afternoon, then fell back below bankfull that night. While out of its banks, minor flooding along parts of Route 26 and Route 260 occurred, primarily in poor drainage areas adjacent to the creek.
